title: Why our brains love lists
titleChinese: 为什么我们的大脑喜欢清单思维？
paragraphs: Productivity can be a struggle for many of us. Overflowing email inboxes, housework, social obligations – it can be easy to feel overwhelmed. However, one simple tool that can help us stay on top of everything is the to-do list. Write it down, do the tasks and cross them off – simple!

There are three key reasons why lists are beneficial, according to psychologist and author David Cohen. Firstly, they help to drown out the chaos and anxiety that comes with having never-ending tasks. By writing everything down, we don't have to rely on our memory and can instead focus on the task at hand. Secondly, lists provide structure and guidance, giving us a plan to follow. As well as this, our brains are more likely to retain information that is presented in a structured and organised manner. And finally, lists serve as proof of what we have achieved, which can help boost our sense of accomplishment and motivation.

Another possible reason our brains love lists is because of something called the 'Zeigarnik Effect'. This is the name psychologists use for when we remember things we need to do, our unfinished tasks, better than things we have already completed. Researchers from Wake Forest University tested the interference of the Zeigarnik effect on a group of people. The experiment began with a warm-up task, though it was stopped half-way through, and only some people were allowed to make plans to finish it. The researchers found that the group permitted to plan had reduced anxiety and performed better in the second task. The problem was, the others still had the warm-up task stuck in their active memory – an unticked list of tasks. So, once we tick something off our list, our brain forgets about it and we can relax.
All in all, it seems lists are a valuable tool for staying on top of life!

vocabulary.entry: **productivity** /ˌprɒdʌkˈtɪvəti/ n. 生产力，效率（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The new software has led to a significant increase in productivity.
vocabulary.translation: 新软件带来了生产力的显著提高。

vocabulary.entry: **overflowing** /ˌəʊvəˈfləʊɪŋ/ adj. 满得溢出的，爆满的
vocabulary.example: Her inbox was overflowing with messages.
vocabulary.translation: 她的收件箱里塞满了邮件。

vocabulary.entry: **obligation** /ˌɒblɪˈɡeɪʃn/ n. 义务，责任（书面语）
vocabulary.example: You are under no obligation to buy anything.
vocabulary.translation: 你不必非得买东西。

vocabulary.entry: **overwhelmed** /ˌəʊvəˈwelmˈd/ adj. 不知所措的，压垮的
vocabulary.example: She felt overwhelmed by the amount of work she had to do.
vocabulary.translation: 她被必须做的大量工作弄得不知所措。

vocabulary.entry: **stay on top of** /ˌsteɪ ɒn ˈtɒp əv/ phr. 掌握，处理（口语）
vocabulary.example: It's hard to stay on top of all the latest news.
vocabulary.translation: 要随时了解所有最新消息很难。

vocabulary.entry: **cross off** /ˌkrɒs ˈɒf/ phr. v. 划掉，删去
vocabulary.example: I crossed his name off the list.
vocabulary.translation: 我把他的名字从名单上划掉了。

vocabulary.entry: **beneficial** /ˌbenɪˈfɪʃl/ adj. 有益的，有利的
vocabulary.example: Regular exercise is beneficial to your health.
vocabulary.translation: 定期锻炼对你的健康有益。

vocabulary.entry: **drown out** /ˌdraʊn ˈaʊt/ phr. v. 淹没（声音），压过
vocabulary.example: The sound of the traffic drowned out her voice.
vocabulary.translation: 交通噪音淹没了她的声音。

vocabulary.entry: **chaos** /ˈkeɪɒs/ n. 混乱，杂乱（书面语）
vocabulary.example: There was total chaos on the roads during the storm.
vocabulary.translation: 暴风雨期间，道路上完全是一片混乱。

vocabulary.entry: **anxiety** /æŋˈzaɪəti/ n. 焦虑，忧虑
vocabulary.example: The exam results caused her a lot of anxiety.
vocabulary.translation: 考试结果让她非常焦虑。

vocabulary.entry: **never-ending** /ˌnevər ˈendɪŋ/ adj. 永无止境的，没完没了的
vocabulary.example: Housework is a never-ending task.
vocabulary.translation: 家务活是永远做不完的事。

vocabulary.entry: **rely on** /rɪˈlaɪ ɒn/ phr. v. 依赖，依靠
vocabulary.example: Many people now rely on the internet for news.
vocabulary.translation: 现在许多人依赖互联网获取新闻。

vocabulary.entry: **at hand** /æt ˈhænd/ phr. 在手边，即将到来
vocabulary.example: Keep your phone close at hand in case of an emergency.
vocabulary.translation: 把电话放在手边以备紧急情况。

vocabulary.entry: **structure** /ˈstrʌktʃə(r)/ n. 结构，体系
vocabulary.example: The essay lacks a clear structure.
vocabulary.translation: 这篇文章缺乏清晰的结构。

vocabulary.entry: **guidance** /ˈɡaɪdns/ n. 指导，引导
vocabulary.example: Children need guidance from their parents.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子需要父母的指导。

vocabulary.entry: **retain** /rɪˈteɪn/ v. 保持，记住（书面语）
vocabulary.example: It's difficult to retain all this information.
vocabulary.translation: 要记住所有这些信息很困难。

vocabulary.entry: **structured** /ˈstrʌktʃəd/ adj. 结构化的，有条理的
vocabulary.example: The course is well-structured and easy to follow.
vocabulary.translation: 这门课程结构合理，易于理解。

vocabulary.entry: **organised** /ˈɔːɡənaɪzd/ adj. 有条理的，有组织的
vocabulary.example: She is a very organised person.
vocabulary.translation: 她是一个非常有条理的人。

vocabulary.entry: **proof** /pruːf/ n. 证据，证明
vocabulary.example: Do you have any proof of your identity?
vocabulary.translation: 你有身份证明吗？

vocabulary.entry: **accomplishment** /əˈkʌmplɪʃmənt/ n. 成就，成绩（书面语）
vocabulary.example: Winning the award was a great accomplishment.
vocabulary.translation: 赢得这个奖项是一项巨大的成就。

vocabulary.entry: **motivation** /ˌməʊtɪˈveɪʃn/ n. 动力，积极性
vocabulary.example: He lacks the motivation to study.
vocabulary.translation: 他缺乏学习的动力。

vocabulary.entry: **interference** /ˌɪntəˈfɪərəns/ n. 干扰，干涉（书面语）
vocabulary.example: The experiment was affected by outside interference.
vocabulary.translation: 实验受到了外部干扰的影响。

vocabulary.entry: **warm-up** /ˈwɔːm ʌp/ n. 热身，准备活动
vocabulary.example: The team did some warm-up exercises before the game.
vocabulary.translation: 球队在赛前做了一些热身运动。

vocabulary.entry: **permitted** /pəˈmɪtɪd/ adj. 被允许的
vocabulary.example: Smoking is not permitted anywhere in the building.
vocabulary.translation: 楼内任何地方都禁止吸烟。

vocabulary.entry: **reduce** /rɪˈdjuːs/ v. 减少，降低
vocabulary.example: The new law will reduce pollution.
vocabulary.translation: 新法律将减少污染。

vocabulary.entry: **perform** /pəˈfɔːm/ v. 表现，执行
vocabulary.example: The team performed well in the competition.
vocabulary.translation: 该队在比赛中表现出色。

vocabulary.entry: **stuck** /stʌk/ adj. 卡住的，无法移动的
vocabulary.example: The key got stuck in the lock.
vocabulary.translation: 钥匙卡在锁里了。

vocabulary.entry: **active memory** /ˈæktɪv ˈmeməri/ n. 活跃记忆，短期记忆
vocabulary.example: The details are still fresh in my active memory.
vocabulary.translation: 细节仍清晰地留在我的记忆中。

vocabulary.entry: **unticked** /ʌnˈtɪkt/ adj. 未打勾的，未勾选的
vocabulary.example: I looked at my unticked to-do list and sighed.
vocabulary.translation: 我看着未勾选的待办事项清单，叹了口气。

vocabulary.entry: **tick off** /ˌtɪk ˈɒf/ phr. v. 打勾标记
vocabulary.example: Tick off each item on the list as you complete it.
vocabulary.translation: 每完成一项就在清单上勾掉。

vocabulary.entry: **all in all** /ˌɔːl ɪn ˈɔːl/ phr. 总而言之，总的来说（口语）
vocabulary.example: All in all, it was a successful event.
vocabulary.translation: 总而言之，这是一次成功的活动。

vocabulary.entry: **valuable** /ˈvæljuəbl/ adj. 宝贵的，有价值的
vocabulary.example: She gave me some valuable advice.
vocabulary.translation: 她给了我一些宝贵的建议。

sentences.english: Productivity can be a struggle for many of us.
sentences.chinese: 对我们许多人来说，保持高效产出可能是一件困难的事。

sentences.english: Overflowing email inboxes, housework, social obligations – it can be easy to feel overwhelmed.
sentences.chinese: 爆满的电子邮件收件箱、家务、社会责任——很容易让人感到不堪重负。

sentences.english: However, one simple tool that can help us stay on top of everything is the to-do list.
sentences.chinese: 然而，一个能帮助我们掌控一切的简单工具就是待办事项清单。

sentences.english: Write it down, do the tasks and cross them off – simple!
sentences.chinese: 写下来，完成任务，然后划掉——简单！

sentences.english: There are three key reasons why lists are beneficial, according to psychologist and author David Cohen.
sentences.chinese: 心理学家兼作家戴维·科恩认为，清单之所以有益，有三个关键原因。

sentences.english: Firstly, they help to drown out the chaos and anxiety that comes with having never-ending tasks.
sentences.chinese: 首先，它们有助于压制因永无止境的任务而产生的混乱和焦虑。

sentences.english: By writing everything down, we don't have to rely on our memory and can instead focus on the task at hand.
sentences.chinese: 通过把所有事情写下来，我们不必依赖记忆，而是可以专注于手头的任务。

sentences.english: Secondly, lists provide structure and guidance, giving us a plan to follow.
sentences.chinese: 其次，清单提供了结构和指导，给了我们一个可以遵循的计划。

sentences.english: As well as this, our brains are more likely to retain information that is presented in a structured and organised manner.
sentences.chinese: 除此之外，我们的大脑更有可能记住以结构化和有组织的方式呈现的信息。

sentences.english: And finally, lists serve as proof of what we have achieved, which can help boost our sense of accomplishment and motivation.
sentences.chinese: 最后，清单可以作为我们已完成事项的证明，这有助于增强我们的成就感和动力。

sentences.english: Another possible reason our brains love lists is because of something called the 'Zeigarnik Effect'.
sentences.chinese: 我们的大脑喜爱清单的另一个可能原因是一种叫做"蔡格尼克效应"的现象。

sentences.english: This is the name psychologists use for when we remember things we need to do, our unfinished tasks, better than things we have already completed.
sentences.chinese: 心理学家用这个名称来描述这一现象：我们更容易记住需要做的事情，即未完成的任务，而不是已经完成的事情。

sentences.english: Researchers from Wake Forest University tested the interference of the Zeigarnik effect on a group of people.
sentences.chinese: 维克森林大学的研究人员测试了蔡格尼克效应对一群人的干扰。

sentences.english: The experiment began with a warm-up task, though it was stopped half-way through, and only some people were allowed to make plans to finish it.
sentences.chinese: 实验从一个热身任务开始，但中途被打断，只允许一部分人制定计划来完成它。

sentences.english: The researchers found that the group permitted to plan had reduced anxiety and performed better in the second task.
sentences.chinese: 研究人员发现，被允许做计划的那一组人的焦虑感有所降低，并且在第二个任务中表现得更好。

sentences.english: The problem was, the others still had the warm-up task stuck in their active memory – an unticked list of tasks.
sentences.chinese: 问题在于，其他人的活跃记忆中仍然卡着那个热身任务——就像一个未勾选的待办事项清单。

sentences.english: So, once we tick something off our list, our brain forgets about it and we can relax.
sentences.chinese: 所以，一旦我们从清单上勾掉某项任务，我们的大脑就会忘记它，我们也就可以放松了。

sentences.english: All in all, it seems lists are a valuable tool for staying on top of life!
sentences.chinese: 总而言之，清单似乎是掌控生活的一个宝贵工具！
